job_description:
Backend Software Engineering Intern — Northstar Software (fictional)
Build and maintain small backend services with a mentor.
Required: Python, SQL, PostgreSQL, REST APIs and Git.
Required: automated testing and collaboration on engineering projects.
Preferred: Docker, Kubernetes and AWS.
Use only supported candidate experience; this simulated position does not imply the candidate has every listed skill.
Preferred: Excel.
source_text:
Alex Example
alex@example.test | Fictional candidate for the CS6983 simulation

INTERESTS
- Organize a weekly campus board game evening.
- Maintain a collection of hiking route notes.
- Photograph local architecture on weekends.
- Help plan the student film society calendar.

EDUCATION
BS in Computer Science, Example University, 2024
Coursework: algorithms, databases and software engineering.

EXPERIENCE
Software Engineering Intern | Example Corp | January–June 2024 (6 months)
- Updated internal onboarding notes for the team.
- Built Python REST endpoints for an internal inventory tool using Postgres and SQL.
- Added unit tests with pytest for input validation.
- Collaborated with two interns and reviewed changes using Git.

PROJECTS
Campus Inventory Demo | Academic project | 2024
- Wrote a short installation guide for classmates.
- Packaged the Python service in Docker for local demonstrations.
- Built a small JS page to display inventory counts.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Python, SQL, Postgres, Git, Docker, JS, pytest

method: Score = 0.8 × weighted requirement coverage + 0.2 × weighted first-evidence prominence. Prominence per match = 1 − nonblank-line rank / max(1, nonblank-line count − 1). Missing requirements receive zero. JD lines containing required/must/essential have weight 2; others weight 1. The same aliases, weights, and requirements are frozen before tailoring.
limitations: Lexical diagnostic, not an ATS score or hiring probability. Curated vocabulary only; no inference of years, seniority, degree equivalence or semantic entailment. Negated/uncertain clauses receive no credit. Tailoring only reorders existing sections/bullets and normalizes explicit technology spellings; it cannot fill qualification gaps. Extracted PDF/DOCX layout is not preserved. Review the text and provenance before use. Indented continuations move with whole claim blocks; ambiguous unindented boundaries freeze the preceding bullet group. Identity and employer metadata are not rewritten. This is not semantic verification of arbitrary resume layouts.
score_interpretation: Presentation/relevance index 72.68 → 79.65; qualification coverage 83.33% → 83.33%. Ordering can change prominence, not candidate qualifications. User constraints take priority over maximizing this index.
